newsitem.title: CHINA: China to continue tight monetary policy - agency.
newsitem.headline: China to continue tight monetary policy - agency.

text.p: China will continue its tight monetary policy in the short term with surging fixed asset investment threatening to revive high inflation, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The agency quoted an unnamed senior official with the State Planning Commission as saying fixed asset investment was expected to exceed 2.3 trillion yuan this year, nearly three times that of 1992.
Since July this year, there has been a resurgence in investment with 700 new fixed asset projects, he said.

The official said that in particular there were too many property projects. In addition, many of the projects were focused on high-class villas and commercial buildings with ordinary residential home construction accounting for less than 60 percent of projects, he said.

"Some regions have persisted in applying for new (fixed asset investment) projects, the pace of investment expansion is still very fast and inflationary pressure is still heavy," the official was quoted as saying.
"Experience since 1993 has proved that if we do not insist on tight monetary policy, high economic growth rates and the downward trend on inflation will be unsustainable," he said.
China's inflation was a year-on-year 14.8 percent last year after hitting a record high of 21 percent in 1994.
Officials estimate inflation will drop to around 6.5 percent this year partly thanks to continued austerity measures in force since July 1993.
The official hinted that Beijing was under pressure to loosen credit, particularly from problem-plagued state-run companies, but added that this was not a good reason to remove controls.

"The current difficulties facing the enterprises cannot be solved through loosening credit," he said. "Otherwise, the economy will overheat again and inflation will be re-ignited, which will in turn add to their difficulties."
